title: 单支节匹配：在离负载 d 处并联一段短路线
statement: 50 Ω 无损耗线（v_p = 3×10⁸ m/s，f = 300 MHz）带负载 Z_L = (30 + j40) Ω。在离负载 d = 0.2917 m 的 J 点并联一段同样的 50 Ω 终端短路线（短截线），长度 l_s 待定。电源 V̇_s = 10∠0° V（有效值），R_s = 50 Ω，经 1.5 m 主线接到 J 点。
并联元件用导纳相加最方便：Y = 1/Z。x 从各段线的始端量起。

questions.ask: 在 J 点向负载看进去（不含短截线）的阻抗 Z_d 的实部 = ?

questions.explain: 化成导纳：Y_d = 1/Z_d = (0.02 + j0.0231) S——实部正好是 1/Z_c，这就是选 d 的依据；只剩电纳 +j0.0231 S 要抵消。

questions.ask: 短路短截线的最短长度 l_s = ?
questions.explain: 短路线输入导纳 Y_s = −j cot(βl_s)/Z_c，令它等于 −j0.0231 S：cot βl_s = 1.155，βl_s = 40.89°，l_s = 40.89/360 × 1 m = 0.1136 m。

questions.ask: 接上短截线后，主线上的驻波比 = ?
questions.explain: Y_J = Y_d + Y_s = 0.02 S = 1/Z_c，主线匹配，VSWR = 1。
电源输出 V_s²/(4R_s) = 0.5 W；短截线是纯电抗，不吸收功率，全部送到 Z_L。

questions.ask: 为什么短截线通常做成终端短路，而不是开路？
choices: 短路端不辐射、长度好调（可以滑动短路块），开路端会有边缘电容和辐射
短路线不能产生容性电纳
开路线的输入阻抗与长度无关
choiceExplain: 短路线在 λ/4 < l_s < λ/2 时就是容性的。
开路线 Z_oc = −jZ_c cot βl，同样随长度变化。
questions.explain: 短路和开路短截线都能产生任意电纳，只是长度差 λ/4；工程上短路端更“理想”，也便于调节。

hints: 先求 J 点向负载看进去的阻抗 Z_d（输入阻抗公式，λ = 1 m），再化成导纳 Y_d = G + jB。
d 选得使 G = 1/Z_c = 0.02 S；短截线只要提供 −jB，就能把总导纳变成 1/Z_c。
终端短路线的输入导纳 Y_s = −j cot(βl_s)/Z_c，解 cot βl_s = B·Z_c，取最短的正解。
solution: **4. 结果。** Y_J = 0.02 S，主线 **VSWR = 1**；负载得到 **0.5 W**。d 和短截线之间那一小段仍有驻波。

en.title: Single-stub matching: a shorted stub in parallel at distance d from the load
statement: A 50 Ω lossless line (v_p = 3×10⁸ m/s, f = 300 MHz) feeds a load Z_L = (30 + j40) Ω. At point J, d = 0.2917 m from the load, an identical 50 Ω line with its end shorted (a stub) of length l_s is connected in parallel. The source V̇_s = 10∠0° V (rms), R_s = 50 Ω reaches J through a 1.5 m main line.
Parallel elements are easiest with admittances: Y = 1/Z. x is measured from the start of each line.

questions.ask: Magnitude of the load reflection coefficient |Γ_L| = ?
Real part of the impedance Z_d seen at J towards the load (without the stub) = ?

questions.explain: As an admittance: Y_d = 1/Z_d = (0.02 + j0.0231) S — the real part is exactly 1/Z_c, which is how d was chosen; only the susceptance +j0.0231 S is left to cancel.

questions.ask: Shortest length of the short-circuited stub l_s = ?
questions.explain: The stub's input admittance is Y_s = −j cot(βl_s)/Z_c; set it to −j0.0231 S: cot βl_s = 1.155, βl_s = 40.89°, l_s = 40.89/360 × 1 m = 0.1136 m.

questions.ask: With the stub connected, the standing-wave ratio on the main line = ?
questions.explain: Y_J = Y_d + Y_s = 0.02 S = 1/Z_c: the main line is matched, VSWR = 1.

questions.ask: Power absorbed by the load P_L = ?
questions.explain: The source delivers V_s²/(4R_s) = 0.5 W; the stub is a pure reactance and absorbs nothing, so all of it reaches Z_L.

questions.ask: Why are stubs usually short-circuited rather than open-circuited?
choices: A short does not radiate and the length is easy to adjust (a sliding short), while an open end has fringing capacitance and radiates
A shorted stub cannot produce a capacitive susceptance
The input impedance of an open stub does not depend on its length
questions.explain: Shorted and open stubs can both give any susceptance — their lengths differ by λ/4; a short is simply closer to ideal in practice and easy to adjust.
choiceExplain: A shorted stub is capacitive for λ/4 < l_s < λ/2.
An open stub has Z_oc = −jZ_c cot βl, which also depends on the length.

hints: First find the impedance Z_d seen at J towards the load (input-impedance formula, λ = 1 m) and convert it to an admittance Y_d = G + jB.
d was chosen so that G = 1/Z_c = 0.02 S; the stub only has to supply −jB to make the total admittance 1/Z_c.
A shorted stub has input admittance Y_s = −j cot(βl_s)/Z_c: solve cot βl_s = B·Z_c and take the shortest positive length.
solution: **4. Result.** Y_J = 0.02 S, main-line **VSWR = 1**; the load receives **0.5 W**. The short piece between J and the load still carries a standing wave.
**Check:** the other solution is d = 0.4583 m (βd = 165°), where Y_d = 0.02 − j0.0231 S and the stub is l_s = 0.3864 m; both make Y_J = 1/Z_c.
